A.text: Oral health is reevaluated at shorter intervals when there is a risk of dry mouth, caries, trismus, or chronic oral GVHD.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

B.text: The 6-month interval is shortened when dry mouth risk is present, so a fixed 6-month schedule is not best.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

C.text: Reevaluation is directed to occur during treatment, not only afterward.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

D.text: Reevaluation is scheduled at regular intervals during treatment rather than being triggered only by symptoms.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

explanation.text: Oral health reevaluation during therapy is routine at 6-month intervals and is made more frequent when dry mouth, caries, trismus, or chronic oral GVHD risk exists.
